## WordResolutionReason type

Why a [resolveWord()](./sh-analysis.resolveword.md) result is `static: false`<!-- -->: the word's exact value cannot be classified as one reliably known literal word.

- `'expansion'` — the word contains a `ParamExp` (`$x`<!-- -->, `${x}`<!-- -->), a `CmdSubst` (command substitution, either `$(...)` or backtick form), an `ArithmExp` (`$((expr))`<!-- -->), or a `ProcSubst` (`<(cmd)`<!-- -->/`>(cmd)`<!-- -->) part: its value depends on program state (variables, command output, process substitution) that only exists at run time. - `'tilde'` — an unquoted, unescaped `~` can trigger tilde expansion. This includes a word-initial tilde, plus eligible tildes after `:` in assignment values or after `=` or `:` in assignment-shaped command arguments. The result depends on the environment or user database. See [ResolveWordOptions.context](./sh-analysis.resolvewordoptions.context.md) for the applicable positions. - `'glob'` — an `ExtGlob` part or possible filename generation from unquoted literal text. The literal check recognizes unescaped `*`<!-- -->, `?`<!-- -->, and `(` for Zsh pattern groups or qualifiers. It also recognizes a bracket expression when an unquoted `[` has a later unquoted `]` in the same word. The result depends on the filesystem at run time. - `'brace'` — the word contains a `BraceExp` part or the pinned upstream `syntax.SplitBraces` produces one on a private observation copy (Bash Reference Manual §3.5.1, "Brace Expansion"). Parser output is unchanged. This reports potential expansion in supporting dialects; a bare Word has no dialect or shell-option state, so even POSIX-parsed words receive the conservative classification. It does not claim POSIX sh expands braces. - `'locale'` — the word contains an ANSI-C Unicode escape for a non-ASCII scalar, whose output depends on the shell locale, or a `$"..."` string translated using the current locale's catalog (Bash Reference Manual §3.1.2.5, "Locale-Specific Translation"). For a locale-translated string, the analyzer checks its `DblQuoted.Dollar` flag before visiting any children, so `$"hi $x"` reports `'locale'`<!-- -->. - `'unsupported'` — the input cannot support an exact Unicode-text claim: an escape crosses caller-constructed word-part boundaries; a brace candidate has escape handling this analyzer cannot trust; a word contains nil/typed nil parts or byte-valued strings; or ANSI-C quoting produces NUL, non-ASCII byte escapes, or non-scalar Unicode escapes (U+D800..U+DFFF or values above U+10FFFF, such as `$'\\uD800'` and `$'\\UFFFFFFFF'`<!-- -->). This analyzer reports exact text only for escapes whose output can be represented faithfully as a JavaScript string.

Reason descriptions do not establish universal precedence among features. Whole-word `unsupported` preflight takes precedence even when a caller has already supplied a `BraceExp`<!-- -->: an escape crossing parts can invalidate the apparent quoting boundaries, and an escape-uncertain brace candidate remains uncertain. Independently quoted or fully protected literal siblings do not suppress a known `BraceExp`<!-- -->. After preflight, existing resolution order can select a triggering tilde or earlier glob before visiting that part.

This union may grow in a \*\*minor\*\* release — new mvdan/sh word-part node types, or new statically-shaped-but-dynamic categories, can add new reason strings without that being a breaking change. It is deliberately not sealed against extension elsewhere in the codebase. A reason string this version of the package doesn't yet know about only ever accompanies `static: false`<!-- -->, never changes the meaning of `static: true`<!-- -->, so runtime consumers that only branch on `.static` are safe by construction across such additions; an exhaustive compile-time `switch` over `.reason` should still include a `default` case to stay forward-compatible.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export type WordResolutionReason =
  "expansion" | "tilde" | "glob" | "brace" | "locale" | "unsupported";
```
